legend: Fibromatosis-like metaplastic carcinoma with focal epithelial differentiation as a diagnostic clue.
An example with chondromyxoid morphology (heterologous mesenchymal differentiation).

Low-grade adenosquamous carcinoma featuring infiltrative glands with bland cytology, focal squamoid differentiation, desmoplastic stroma, and lymphoid aggregates. Some infiltrating glands may show peripheral myoepithelial-like cells.
Low-grade adenosquamous carcinoma. Core biopsy shows a frankly invasive lesion on H&E section.

Low-grade adenosquamous carcinoma. CK5/6 expression in this core biopsy (see Fig. <<#48394>> for H&E) is strong and diffuse, particularly in the foci with squamous differentiation. The pattern of staining is different from the mosaic pattern of the hyperplastic epithelial lesions.

A case of metaplastic matrix-producing carcinoma showing high-grade cytonuclear features, with dyscohesive cells in a chondroid matrix. The degree of atypia in these tumours can be variable. Although the presence of the cartilaginous/chondroid matrix is pathognomonic of these tumours, its amount and distribution can be heterogeneous.

High-grade spindle cell metaplastic carcinoma associated with high-grade cribriform non–spindle cell type ductal carcinoma in situ, supporting the carcinomatous nature of the invasive spindle cell component.
The neoplastic cells are positive for high-molecular-weight cytokeratin. (34βE12 immunohistochemistry)
The breast core biopsy shows a low-grade spindle cell proliferation infiltrating the adipose tissue, resembling fibromatosis.
The tumour is composed of compressed glandular structures, with low-grade features, infiltrating the stroma, and scattered nests of squamous cells and squamous cysts.
A high-grade metaplastic carcinoma characterized by sheets of epithelial tumour cells embedded within a chondroid matrix.

diagnosis: Metaplastic carcinoma, matrix-producing type, with osseous differentiation
legend: A high-grade carcinoma with prominent osteoid production. There is a focal component of invasive carcinoma of no special type (NST), supporting the diagnosis of metaplastic carcinoma.
Immunohistochemistry reveals positivity for high-molecular-weight cytokeratin. (34βE12 immunohistochemistry)
A spindle cell neoplasm with high-grade cytological atypia and increased mitotic activity.
A metaplastic carcinoma characterized by malignant squamous cells with marked nuclear atypia.

diagnosis: Gross photo of a metaplastic spindle cell carcinoma
legend: A firm, relatively circumscribed mass with focally infiltrative borders. The cut surface is tan-white with areas of necrosis and haemorrhage.
Metaplastic carcinoma with squamous cell features shows pavemented anastomosing islands of plump polygonal and spindle cells with focal keratinisation. Necrosis and calcifications are noted.

Low grade adenosquamous carcinoma shows small squamoid nests and plump spindle cells within serpiginous fibrotic zones among ducts with moderate to florid usual ductal hyperplasia. Some nests show small lumens. The elongated epithelial nests merge into the spindle cell background which sometimes forms a spindle cell cuff around the nests.

Fibromatosis-like metaplastic carcinoma shows a hyalinised collagenous stroma with scattered, more cellular foci of plump spindle cells with mild nuclear atypia. The spindle cells are positive for CK5/6, CK14 and p63 by immunohistochemistry.

Spindle cell metaplastic carcinoma of variable cellularity, irregularly invading into the fibroadipose stroma. Scattered benign ducts are found within the tumour. Spindle cell population is diffusely reactive for epithelial markers Cam5.2 and MNF116 by immunohistochemistry.

diagnosis: Invasive carcinoma with spindle cell metaplastic and poorly differentiated neuroendocrine components, grade 3.
legend:
Invasive carcinoma with spindle cell metaplastic and poorly differentiated neuroendocrine components, grade 3:
Breast core biopsies from a 93-year-old female show two distinct tumour components. The first component comprises a malignant spindle cell proliferation disclosing hyperchromatic, pleomorphic and sometimes multinucleated nuclei. Brisk mitotic activity (reaching 15 per 10 high power fields, field diameter 0.66 mm), areas of infarction and entrapped nerves are present.
The second component shows a poorly differentiated carcinoma arranged in sheets, with malignant cells disclosing round to ovoid hyperchromatic nuclei, indistinct nucleoli and scant cytoplasm. Brisk mitotic activity, (reaching 40 per 10 high power fields, field diameter= 0.66 mm), lymphovascular invasion and pockets of tumour necrosis are noted. 
Both components are triple negative and show scattered staining for epithelial markers, with the poorly differentiated carcinoma disclosing diffuse synaptophysin reactivity supporting neuroendocrine differentiation (immunohistochemistry not shown).
